articles.title: Putin’s residence in Valdai has been surrounded by a second ring of air defenses — the number of positions has exceeded 50
articles.body:
Putin’s residence in Valdai has been surrounded by a second ring of air defenses — the number of positions has exceeded 50
Kyiv • UNN
More than 50 air defense positions have been identified within a 50-kilometer radius of Putin’s residence. In October alone, 15 new towers appeared on the Ukrainian side.
A second air defense ring has been built around the residence of Russian dictator Vladimir Putin in Valdai. There are already more than 50 air defense positions within a 50-kilometer radius of the estate. The Moscow Times reports this, citing satellite imagery, writes UNN.
Details
In October alone, more than 15 new towers for deploying Pantsir or Tor anti-aircraft systems appeared south of the residence, on the side facing Ukraine.
Since April, the number of air defense positions around the estate has doubled. For comparison, in Moscow and the Moscow region, where more than 20 million people live, only approximately twice as many such positions were built after the start of the full-scale invasion.
The Kremlin strengthens security around the residence
At the end of December 2025, Russia accused Ukraine of allegedly attacking Putin's residence with 91 drones. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called these claims fake.
After this, the Russian authorities began strengthening security at the site. In particular, in the summer, anti-drone nets began to be installed over the road leading to the residence.
According to journalistic investigations, Putin and his close associates had regularly used the residence in the past, but recently may have stopped traveling there due to concerns for their own safety.

articles.title: Trump rules out Sunday strike on Iran as Netanyahu warns Israel faces imminent existential threat
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump said Sunday that the United States would not launch a military strike against Iran today.
Asked by a reporter whether a US attack on Iran could take place as soon as today, Trump replied: “Would I tell you that? The answer is no. There will not be a strike today.”
The president did not rule out military action at a later date.
Earlier on Sunday, Trump told reporters that he has yet to make a decision on whether or not to renew strikes against Iran.
“Should I finish the job - which would be very easy to do - or should I reach an agreement? That is the whole decision," he said.
Trump says 'not much going on' at Iranian nuclear sites, Netanyahu claims Israel facing existential threat
Trump added that the US is actively monitoring activity at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site as well as three other sites that were allegedly destroyed in previous strikes.
“There isn’t much activity going on there,” he clarified.
Trump’s comments came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in a post on X/Twitter that Israel is currently facing “real and tangible existential danger” coming from Iran.
Netanyahu claimed that only a small window of time remains for Israel and the US to act and completely defeat Iran.
Netanyahu also shared a video from one of the IDF's anti-missile batteries where he said: "The IDF is prepared on both defense and in offense. I warn our enemies – you will absorb strikes out of proportion, stronger than you can even imagine."
Trump said on Friday that Washington is weighing another military operation against Iran, saying that the US “may do another little Epic Fury” during a pre-midterm election rally in Florida.

articles.title: Iran slams US-Israeli attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities, condemns double standards
articles.body:
Iran slams US-Israeli attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities, condemns double standards
TEHRAN– Iran’s ambassador to the United Nations has condemned US and Israeli attacks on Iran’s peaceful nuclear facilities, accusing Western countries and international nuclear authorities of applying double standards and politicizing global non-proliferation efforts.
Addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York on Friday, Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran’s ambassador and deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, reaffirmed Iran’s inalienable right under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) to develop nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, including uranium enrichment.
Darzi said the United States was challenging the rights of NPT member states by questioning their entitlement to pursue the full nuclear fuel cycle. He argued that denying countries access to uranium enrichment technology while claiming to support peaceful nuclear energy was incompatible with Article IV of the treaty.
“No State can unilaterally rewrite the Treaty or impose its own political veto on the legitimate rights of other States Parties,” he said, warning against the use of non-proliferation concerns as a means of exerting political pressure on sovereign nations.
The Iranian envoy said the United States and Israel had launched two wars of aggression against Iran in 2025 and 2026, targeting its peaceful nuclear facilities under International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards. He described the attacks as violations of international law, the UN Charter, the IAEA Statute, relevant IAEA General Conference resolutions and UN Security Council Resolution 487 (1981).
According to Darzi, the attacks caused extensive destruction and claimed thousands of lives, including that of Iran’s Leader, whose religious decree, or fatwa, rejects nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction.
Iran criticizes international response
Darzi strongly criticized the IAEA’s governing bodies, its director general and the UN Security Council for failing to condemn the attacks on safeguarded nuclear facilities. He said the absence of a clear response had exposed the selective application of international non-proliferation standards.
“Instead, pressure is directed against the victim while the aggressors escape accountability,” he said.
The envoy contrasted the treatment of Iran, an NPT member since 1970, with that of Israel, which he described as the only nuclear-armed state in the region and whose nuclear facilities are not subject to comprehensive IAEA safeguards.
He argued that continued political and military pressure on Iran, alongside 'impunity for Israel,' undermined the credibility of the international non-proliferation regime. He also criticized the withholding of technical cooperation that, in his view, deprived Iran of the benefits of peaceful nuclear development that the IAEA is mandated to promote.
Safety conditions remain central to inspections
Addressing calls for the resumption of inspections, Darzi said Iran had neither abandoned nor formally suspended its safeguards obligations. However, he stressed that the military attacks had fundamentally changed the physical and security conditions under which verification activities could take place.
He noted that the IAEA’s own reports acknowledged that verification activities had ceased and inspectors had been withdrawn for safety reasons. Such concerns, he said, could not be disregarded when demands were made for their return.
“No country can reasonably be expected to provide access amid military operations and persistent threats without adequate safety guarantees,” Darzi said, adding that responsibility for creating these conditions rested with the countries that carried out the attacks.
He concluded that Iran remained prepared to cooperate with the IAEA to the extent permitted by prevailing circumstances, but emphasized that such cooperation must not compromise the safety of the Iranian people, nuclear facilities or agency inspectors.
Darzi also insisted that the IAEA’s reporting must remain professional, objective and free from political influence, arguing that the agency’s credibility depended on technical integrity and impartiality.

articles.title: Putin dismisses claims Russia is fueling European protests as ‘clear overkill’
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has dismissed accusations that Moscow is orchestrating mass protests in major European cities as a “clear overkill,” accusing European leaders of blaming external powers rather than confronting the causes of domestic unrest.
In an interview with the VGTRK broadcasting company published on Sunday, Putin said he was initially surprised that European criticism over the demonstrations focused on the United States before shifting towards Russia.
“Claims immediately began to be thrown out that the events taking place in Europe are the result of the activities of the current American administration and its support for right-wing parties and movements,” he said.
Putin described that reaction as “strange and completely unexpected,” saying he had not anticipated European leaders would criticise the United States, which he called their main military ally and protector.
He added that European leaders had subsequently returned to what he described as their “traditional accusations” against Russia.
Putin accuses European leaders of shifting blame
Putin argued that allegations of Russian involvement in mass demonstrations were exaggerated and said European governments were avoiding responsibility for the unrest.
“My first reaction when I saw this was surprise, because to say that we are provoking mass protests in major European cities is a clear overkill,” he said, adding that the claim should be obvious to ordinary European citizens.
The Russian president said the accusations reflected what he described as the weakness of some European leaders, arguing that they were blaming Washington and Moscow rather than analysing the underlying causes of public discontent.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected allegations of Russian interference in European political affairs.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov also dismissed the accusations as “absurd” on October 19, according to reports.
France protests fuel dispute over foreign influence
The remarks come amid weeks of nationwide student protests in France, where debate over the demonstrations has increasingly extended to allegations of outside influence.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, speaking at an Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development-hosted conference on October 21, accused protesters of drawing on what he described as “hostile narratives” associated with Russia, China, Iran and the MAGA movement.

articles.title: Thousands protest against Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Thousands protest against Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election (VIDEO)
A major protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has taken place in Tel-Aviv just days ahead of the Israeli parliamentary election on October 27.
A square outside the Museum of Art in the country’s largest city was packed on Saturday evening, with the demonstrators holding national flags and banners, reading ‘Change will come’, ‘No more Mr. Far Right Guy’ and other slogans.
The organizers of the gathering from the October Council group put the attendance at over 100,000. The police have yet to announce official figures.
Netanyahu’s main rival in the election – Yashar party chairman and former military chief of staff, Gadi Eisenkot – and other leaders of the opposition bloc have attended the rally. The crowd cheered Eisenkot’s appearance, chanting: “Who’s coming? The next prime minister.”
The October Council was formed by families of the victims of the attack on Israel by Hamas on October 7, 2023, who demand accountability from Netanuahy’s right-wing government for the failure to prevent the incursion.
Saturday’s protest, organized with the title ‘In Three Days, Vote for a State Commission of Inquiry’, is the culmination of three years of weekly rallies, according to the group.
The State Commissions of Inquiry, which are independent panels appointed by the Supreme Court, are usually set up in Israel to investigate major failures by the authorities. However, Netanyahu refused to establish such a probe into October 7, insisting that it would be biased against his government.
Reports in the US and local media claimed that the prime minister ignored warnings of the planned attack by Hamas he had received from various sources, including Israeli intelligence and the UAE and Egypt. Netanyahu has denied those claims.
A poll by public broadcaster KAN published before the start of the election silence period on Friday, suggested that Eisenkot’s opposition bloc would get 52 out of 120 in the Israeli parliament, with Netanyahu and his supporters winning 50 seats. This means that neither is likely control the Knesset outright.
Israel responded to the October 7 incursion by Hamas, in which 1,200 people lost their lives and around 250 were taken hostage, by launching a military campaign in Gaza.
Israeli airstrikes and a ground offensive have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children, and injured over 175,000 others in the enclave over the past three years, according to the local Health Ministry. More than 1,500 deaths happened after a US-brokered ceasefire went into effect in October 2025.

articles.title: “Strasbourg Calling”: Europe must produce the right things, not simply more
articles.body:
Author
Irina Nedeva
Interview
German MEP from the Greens Danie Freund:
“Strasbourg Calling”: Europe must produce the right things, not simply more
Interview with MEP Daniel Freund
Sunday 25 October 2026 13:06
Sunday, 25 October 2026, 13:06
MEP Daniel Freund
PHOTO Irina Nedeva
Font size
At its Strasbourg session this week, the European Parliament discussed the conclusions of last week's European Council meeting. However, the major issue of the EU's long-term budget for 2028-2034 remains unresolved. Europe wants to become a geopolitical power, rearm, compete with China and maintain its climate targets. But who will pay for it all?
German Green MEP Daniel Freund, the Greens' coordinator on the Committee on Budgetary Control, warns that Europe cannot take on more responsibilities with less money and must not abandon its climate targets.
Speaking on BNR's special  broadcast from Strasbourg, he said:
“Europe still has a great deal to do in terms of defence, support for Ukraine and competition with China. I see our chancellor, as well as members of my own party, calling for substantial budget cuts. Fuel prices keep rising, driven by our dependence on fossil fuels and the problems involving Iran.
I think we are currently seeing some of the highest prices ever at petrol pumps and filling stations. At the same time, we are seeing a major increase in electric vehicle use. In Denmark, for example, electric vehicles already account for 80% of new car sales, while in Germany the figure is 30%. So I think we need to move in that direction.”
MEP Daniel Freund and BNR's Irina Nedeva in the Radio Studios complex at the European Parliament in Strasbourg (21 October 2026)
PHOTO Rositsa Petkova
Italy, Greece, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia are preparing a petition calling for a further postponement or weakening of the emissions trading scheme. Europe must nevertheless maintain its climate targets, the politician insisted in an interview with BNR Horizon's programme “Strasbourg Calling”:
“We do not want to keep spending billions to support petrol producers, these huge companies, and in doing so also support dictators. We want to put an end to that! We want to continue transforming our economies and making them increasingly green. This summer, we saw 32,000 Europeans lose their lives during heatwaves. And yet it was the coolest summer compared with those forecast to come. So we certainly need to keep moving in this direction.”
Daniel Freund argued that decarbonisation is not incompatible with industrial competitiveness:
“We can already see what is happening in China. The Chinese market has stopped buying cars with internal combustion engines from us, and only electric vehicles are being used. The same applies to other products. So if we want to remain competitive, we need to offer the right products. For example, companies that use electric trucks and renewable energy are not currently being affected by the fuel crisis.”
Europe must strengthen its defence industry, but even defence is becoming greener, he noted:
“Even if we look at the battlefield in Ukraine, we can see that this war is being fought, to some extent, using renewable energy. A large number of drones are being deployed, and they operate on batteries. What we must do is stand together in defending Ukraine, because in doing so we are fighting for our shared values and our own survival.”
The Greens will support the European Parliament resolution aimed at strengthening security in the Black Sea in response to Russian threats, he added:
“I think we will support the resolution. We stand with Bulgaria, Romania and every country that falls victim to such Russian attacks.”

articles.title: Twelve countries condemn any attack or threat against nuclear facilities
articles.body:
Twelve countries condemn any attack or threat against nuclear facilities
TEHRAN – Twelve countries, including Iran, Russia, China and Pakistan, have issued a joint statement declaring that nuclear facilities must never, under any circumstances, be subjected to attack or the threat of attack.
On Friday, the 12 countries — Belarus, Burkina Faso, China, Cuba, Eritrea, Iran, Nicaragua, Niger, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Zimbabwe — issued the joint statement during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly’s First Committee. The statement addressed the prohibition of any attack or threat of attack against nuclear sites and facilities that are under the safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and dedicated to peaceful purposes.
According to IRNA, the statement was read out by Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran’s ambassador and chargé d’affaires to the United Nations. It contained eight points, as follows:
1. We reaffirm the importance of the full and effective fulfilment of the objectives of the International Atomic Energy Agency, particularly its statutory mission to accelerate and enlarge the contribution of atomic energy to peace, health and prosperity throughout the world. We also reaffirm the inalienable right of all states to develop research into, produce and use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes without discrimination.
2. We recall United Nations Security Council Resolution 487 (1981), which strongly condemned a military attack against nuclear facilities. We also recall the relevant decisions and resolutions of the IAEA General Conference — documents GC(53)/DEC/13, GC(XXIX)/RES/443, GC(XXIX)/RES/444 and GC(XXXIV)/RES/533 — which clearly reflect the longstanding position of the international community opposing any attack or threat of attack against nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards and dedicated to peaceful purposes.
3. We reaffirm that an attack or threat of attack against nuclear facilities violates the principles of the United Nations Charter, international law and the Statute of the International Atomic Energy Agency, and is fundamentally incompatible with the objectives and purposes of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT).
4. We emphasize that attacks against nuclear facilities have serious implications for nuclear safety and security and pose a grave threat to the integrity, effectiveness and credibility of the IAEA safeguards system, as well as to the broader global non-proliferation framework.
5. We emphasize that attacks against nuclear facilities would adversely affect the peaceful uses of nuclear energy and international cooperation, and could result in the release of radioactive materials, with severe consequences both within and beyond the affected country, including serious impacts on civilian populations and long-term environmental damage.
6. We emphasize that silence in the face of attacks against protected nuclear facilities undermines established international norms, erodes confidence in the international legal order and increases the risk of such attacks becoming normalised.
7. We therefore reaffirm that nuclear facilities must never, under any circumstances, be subjected to attack or the threat of attack.
8. We call on all member states to stand united in preserving the integrity and credibility of the IAEA safeguards system, strengthening nuclear safety and security, and protecting the peaceful uses of nuclear energy and international cooperation by expressing their clear and unequivocal opposition to any attack or threat of attack against nuclear facilities.

articles.title: EU extends sanctions against Jacques Baud
articles.body:
EU extends sanctions against Jacques Baud
The European Union has extended the sanctions against Jacques Baud, a former colonel in the Swiss Army General Staff, who is accused of spreading pro-Russian propaganda, until October 9, 2027. He remains subject to an asset freeze and travel restrictions.
According to official EU documents reported by the French-speaking Swiss online media outlet L’Impertinent, on October 8 the Council of the European Union renewed the sanctions regime against Russia’s “destabilising activities”, which targets 80 individuals and 20 entities.
Added to this list on December 15, 2025, the 71-year-old Brussels resident is accused of his contributions to media outlets described as pro-Russian and of spreading “conspiracy theories”. The EU Council criticises him in particular for accusing Ukraine of having orchestrated its own invasion in order to join NATO.
Initially, Brussels accused him of supporting Russian actions that “undermine or threaten the stability or security of a third country (Ukraine)”. The new text now refers to actions that “undermine democracy and threaten the stability or security of a third country”. Ukraine is no longer explicitly mentioned, and the conjunction “or” has been replaced by “and”. The specific allegations remain unchanged. The EU has not provided any justification for the rewording.
The individual concerned disputes the allegations: “I have never received a single cent from Russia,” he stated in December 2025, notably in an interview with L’Impertinent. The 71-year-old claims to base his analyses on Ukrainian and American sources and disputes, in particular, the interpretation of his statements regarding the Russian invasion. In his view, these statements referred to an interview given in 2019 by Oleksiy Arestovych, who was to become an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Baud brought a case before the General Court of the EU last March seeking the annulment of his inclusion on the list.
+ Switzerland approves 20th sanctions package against Russia
A retired colonel of the General Staff, born in Geneva, Jacques Baud worked for the Swiss secret services from 1983 to 1990, where he was responsible for analysing Warsaw Pact forces. He subsequently held various posts with the UN, notably in Sudan.
Highly critical of the EU’s and Western countries’ policies on the war in Ukraine, Baud has a large online following, particularly on YouTube, where his videos have racked up several million views.
The sanctions are having a serious impact on his daily life. Baud can no longer freely access his bank accounts, particularly to access his pension. He also claims he is unable to leave Belgium.
After several months of restrictions, a humanitarian exemption had allowed him to regain access to his Belgian account from mid-March to the end of June. Since the beginning of July, he says, the funds have once again been inaccessible. A new exemption requested at the start of May was granted by the Belgian authorities at the start of October, but by the middle of the month it had still not been implemented.

articles.title: Druze experts condemn Tom Barrack's accusations against Syrian Druze, warn of sectarian violence
articles.body:
US envoy Tom Barrack’s claims that the area between Sweida and Daraa was “the captagon manufacturing operation of the world” and that a Druze sheikh was using perceived American and Israeli backing to “persecute other Druze” have drawn criticism from the Druze community, with some Israeli experts telling The Jerusalem Post on Sunday that the remarks had led them to question his suitability for the role.
Speaking in an interview with Lebanese-Australian podcaster Mario Nawfal on Friday, Barrack alleged that Druze in the area were living off the manufacture and sale of illicit drugs.
“It’s not Israel that worries me. It’s a particular Druze sheikh who utilizes the perception of Israeli backing of some alignment with America to persecute other Druze,” Barrack said.
Although Barrack did not name the sheikh, his comments have been widely interpreted in Arab media as referring to Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri, a spiritual leader of the Druze community who has called for Israeli support and independence from Syria.
Growing calls for Syrian Druze independence
Calls for independence and Israeli support among Syria’s Druze community have grown more frequent since Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power in late 2024.
Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham, the formerly designated terrorist organization led by Sharaa, has a documented history of persecuting Druze, while the sectarian massacres in July 2025 and sporadic violence since have further fueled fears of Damascus’s Islamist government.
Against this backdrop, Israeli Druze diplomat and historian Dr. Reda Mansour criticized Barrack’s remarks in a post on X/Twitter, describing his attribution of the global Captagon trade to the Druze region and his criticism of its local leadership as “highly irresponsible” and untruthful.
“By baselessly criminalizing an entire ethnic minority, these statements put the vulnerable Druze community in southern Syria at direct risk of sectarian violence and targeted jihadi attacks. Painting a minority enclave as an illicit hub paints a dangerous target on their back for extremist networks,” Mansour wrote.
“Diplomacy demands accuracy, not reckless generalizations that compromise human lives. We stand in solidarity with the Druze community in Syria.”
Concerns rise amid ongoing violence against Druze community
Mansour’s concerns come amid continued violence against the community. More than 1,300 Druze were killed in the July 2025 massacres in Sweida and surrounding villages, according to UN figures, while subsequent outbreaks of sectarian violence have continued to see civilians abducted and killed.
Civilians have also been killed in Jordanian military strikes on facilities Amman alleges are used for weapons storage and drug manufacturing. In a strike on January 18, 2024, for example, Jordan killed sisters Farah and Dima, aged three and five, along with their parents and other members of their extended family.
Dr. Mordechai Kedar, a research fellow at the Begin-Sadat Center for Strategic Studies, told the Post that Barrack’s comments and “lack of understanding” of the region have “brought a lot of damage to the whole Middle East.”
Doubting Barrack’s knowledge of the issue of Sweida or the sectarian violence, Kedar said that he thought Barrack was relying on information provided to him and not the information on the ground or from the people affected by the violence.
Jonathan Hessen, a senior fellow at the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security, added that Barrack’s remarks were not just “dismaying” because they showed a disregard for the safety and security of a community that has already been subjected to multiple massacres but because his statements were factually unfounded.
“Even when the Jordanians launched airstrikes in southern Syria, the majority of the targeted warehouses were actually in Daraa, the province south of Sweida, where the Bedouins reside,” he said.
“One warehouse was also targeted in Sweida, although I am not aware of its contents. However, those targets were provided to the Jordanians by Damascus, so there are certain aspects that need to be taken into account.”
He noted that Barrack has a pattern of minimizing the suffering of those across the Middle East where the impact would disrupt his broader plans, referencing both Barrack’s comments last week, where he insisted that the Islamic regime was “not evil,” and past commentary on Syrian violence.

articles.title: Europe should be included in Ukraine peace discussions, Kremlin aide says
articles.body:
Europe should be included in discussions on a peace settlement in Ukraine because its position could be crucial, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said on Sunday.
The US has been unable to put pressure on Kyiv to agree to a peace deal, Ushakov said in an interview with state television correspondent Pavel Zarubin.
"Before, it seemed after Anchorage that the US administration might be able to dictate something and force Kyiv to comply. But so far, this hasn't really worked out," Ushakov said, referring to a 2025 meeting in Anchorage between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"That's because it's not enough to talk only to Kyiv; we need to talk to the whole of Europe, which fully supports Kyiv."
EU makes cautious approaches to Russia
After initially leaving it to Trump to try to broker an end to Russia's war in Ukraine, the EU has made cautious approaches to Russia. The leaders of Britain, Germany and France have said they support a proposal for talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Putin to secure a ceasefire, and that Europe would play a role.
Russia, meanwhile, has said it would be open to dialogue but not ultimatums.
On Sunday, Ushakov said Russia was ready to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the US after Russia's National Unity Day on November 4, echoing Kremlin comments this week that Putin's willing to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine as soon as next month.
Zelensky said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of their leaders would follow.
Ushakov also commented on a potential meeting between Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Trump, saying that preparations had already started. The proposed meeting is set to be held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China over November 18-19.
Ushakov said a separate meeting between Putin and Trump in Shenzhen had not been agreed upon.

articles.title: Russian embassy denies reports of staff leaving Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant
articles.body:
Russian embassy denies reports of staff leaving Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant
TEHRAN – The Russian Embassy in Tehran has dismissed reports that Russian diplomatic staff and specialists working at Iran’s Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant are leaving the country, stressing that activities are continuing as usual.
In a statement, the embassy said it was aware of reports published by certain hostile media outlets alleging that an evacuation of Russian embassy personnel and specialists at the Bushehr facility was underway.
“We would like to clarify that neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant are leaving Iran,” the statement said.
The embassy emphasized that operations were proceeding as normal, describing contrary reports as false information and saying their origins were entirely clear.
Located on Iran’s southern coast along the Persian Gulf, the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant is Iran’s first commercial nuclear power facility. Although construction at the site was initially undertaken by the German company Siemens in the 1970s, Russia took responsibility for completing the plant’s first reactor unit under an agreement signed with Iran in the 1990s. The first unit was connected to Iran’s national electricity grid in 2011 and reached full capacity in 2013.
Russia has continued to cooperate with Iran on the development of the facility, including the construction of additional reactor units. The project forms part of broader cooperation between Tehran and Moscow in the peaceful use of nuclear energy.

articles.title: IDF kills two terrorists who funneled millions from Iran and Turkey to Hamas
articles.body:
The IDF announced Sunday that it had killed two terrorists in separate airstrikes in the Gaza Strip last week, accusing them of transferring millions of shekels from Iran and Turkey to Hamas' military wing throughout the war. According to the military, the funds were used to help the terrorist organization rebuild its military capabilities and prepare attacks against Israeli soldiers and civilians.
The first terrorist, Alaa Ibrahim Nimer Arshi, a cell commander in Hamas' military wing, was killed in an airstrike in the Gaza City area. The second, Karam Riyad Hassan Abu Butaihan, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorist who helped transfer money to Hamas, was killed in the Nuseirat area in central Gaza.
According to the IDF, both men played a role in channeling funds to Hamas throughout the war, including money originating from Iran and Turkey. The military said the financial transfers had recently supported Hamas' efforts to restore its military infrastructure and advance attacks against Israeli forces and civilians.
In a separate operation last week, the IDF and Shin Bet security agency carried out an airstrike in central Gaza, destroying a weapons depot used by Hamas to store military equipment. The facility contained Kalashnikov rifles, a launcher and rockets, according to the military.
Additional terrorists killed in Gaza strikes
The announcement follows an IDF statement last week confirming the deaths of two additional terrorists in separate strikes.
One was Akram Bassam Shaaban Yassin, a senior member of Hamas' General Security apparatus in the Gaza Strip. The other was Tamer Mohammed Ibrahim al-Sabbagh, whom the military identified as a member of the terrorist cell responsible for abducting and murdering German-Israeli citizen Shani Louk during the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel.

articles.title: Russian Strike Hits Epicentr Mall in Poltava, Woman Injured
articles.body:
A Russian aerial strike struck the Epicentr shopping center in the central city of Poltava on Sunday, Oct. 25, igniting a fire across the commercial building and injuring a 52-year-old woman, regional authorities reported.
Head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration Vitalii Diakivnych announced on Telegram that incoming fire struck the large retail center, triggering an immediate blaze and causing structural damage.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“A fire broke out. Information regarding the extent of the damage is being clarified. Liquidation of the consequences of the attack is ongoing. Preliminarily, a 52-year-old woman sustained injuries,” Diakivnych stated.
Emergency responders, specialized firefighting brigades, and civil defense units deployed to the site of the hit to contain the blaze, secure the perimeter, and evaluate whether additional personnel or visitors were inside the facility during the impact.
Weekend infrastructure strikes
The kinetic impact on the Epicentr hypermarket in Poltava follows a sequence of targeted Russian strikes against commercial retail sites, logistics facilities, and public infrastructure across Ukraine over the weekend.
On Saturday evening, Russian forces struck a commercial shopping center in the Osnovianskyi district of Kharkiv, igniting a major structural blaze, alongside strikes on a construction hypermarket and industrial facilities that wounded several civilians and three emergency rescue workers during follow-on secondary strikes.
4 Killed in Synelnykove Strike, Rescuers Hit in Kharkiv
Concurrently in Dnipropetrovsk region, a strike drone hit a residential high-rise in Synelnykove, killing four civilians and wounding 13 others.
Overnight into Sunday, Russian bombardments damaged critical infrastructure and municipal utility networks across nine regions, with impacts reported at thermal power plants, electrical substations, coal mining enterprises, grain storage facilities, and a postal depot.

articles.title: Trump wants 'business with both' Ukraine, Russia after war ends
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Oct. 24 that he sees the U.S. doing business with both Ukraine and Russia after the war ends, despite criticism of efforts to restore commercial ties with Moscow.
The statement comes as the first tanker carrying Russian diesel is heading to New York from the Baltic port of Primorsk, set to deliver 40,000 metric tons of fuel following a supply agreement Trump announced on Oct. 9.
Soon after the announcement, Moscow partially lifted restrictions on its diesel exports, permitting the sale of 500,000 metric tons.
"Certainly, we'll do business with Ukraine and with Russia after this war ends, I would think," Trump said.
Trump added that he wanted to "get back to life where Russia and Ukraine make a deal, and then we'd be able to do business with both."
The U.S. president also argued that Washington should have secured greater financial returns in exchange for the billions of dollars in aid provided to Kyiv during Joe Biden's presidency.
"I feel foolish because all you had to do is ask them, and they would have paid. Meaning the EU would have paid," Trump said.
Plans to import around 900,000 metric tons of Russian diesel in the coming months have drawn criticism of the Trump administration from European allies, Ukraine, and members of Congress, as the shipments would circumvent sanctions imposed on Moscow over its war against Ukraine.
The shipment would mark the first Russian diesel deliveries to the U.S. since 2022, when then-President Joe Biden banned imports of Russian oil and petroleum products in response to Russia's war against Ukraine.
The deal comes amid a growing rift between Kyiv and Washington, as Ukraine faces restrictions on Starlink access and reported delays in deliveries of Patriot air defense interceptors.
Trump has also stepped up his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, accusing him of being unwilling to end the war and calling for his replacement.
The decision to resume Russian diesel imports coincides with a challenging political landscape for Republicans ahead of the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, with recent polls showing declining support for Trump.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll found that just 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance, marking the lowest approval rating of either of his presidential terms.
Meanwhile, 47% of registered voters said they would vote for Democrats if congressional elections were held today, compared with 35% who favored Republicans, giving Democrats a 12-point lead — their largest of the current election cycle.

articles.title: Iraq braces for renewed Iran conflict after 1,000 strikes on Kurdistan, 600 militia attacks
articles.body:
Iraq is on edge over the prospect of renewed fighting with Iran after Tehran carried out some 1,000 strikes on the Kurdistan Region in northern Iraq. Additionally, Iranian-backed militias launched roughly 600 attacks inside Iraq, most of them on US diplomatic facilities.
Iraq closed some border crossings with Iran, including the Al-Sheeb crossing in southern Iraq, on Wednesday, saying it needed upgrades to security and technical infrastructure. Iran criticized the decision, saying Baghdad failed to provide advance notice and rejected allegations that narcotics and counterfeit currency are being smuggled into Iraq through border crossings, according to a Rudaw report.
This crossing, also known as Al-Shaib, was the first targeted for closure in Maysan Governorate. This crossing is believed to be near an area where an Iranian-backed militia in Iraq launched a drone strike on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline in September. Rudaw also reported that, in retaliation, Iranian businessman Babak Zanjani called for restrictions on Iraqi oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
Meanwhile, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has denied reports that Ukrainian forces, military units or drones are operating from its territory. The KRG Interior Ministry issued a statement on Thursday rejecting the allegations as baseless, according to the Iraqi News Agency (INA). However, the source of the reports remains unclear.
The ministry emphasized that the Kurdistan region maintains a policy of neutrality in regional and international conflicts. It said it would not allow its territory to serve as a base for hostile military operations against other countries. The statement reflects the KRG's efforts to avoid being sucked into conflicts involving Iran, as Tehran has been pressuring Iraq to expel Kurdish-Iranian opposition groups that are present in the Kurdistan region of northern Iraq.
Iraq, Jordan move to strengthen bilateral security
In another development, Iraq and Jordan have emphasized the importance of strengthening bilateral security cooperation. According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Iraqi Interior Minister Yasser al-Maliki spoke by telephone on Wednesday with his Jordanian counterpart, Mazen al-Faraya. Faraya congratulated Maliki on assuming his new position, and the two officials discussed expanding coordination between their interior ministries.
The Iraqi Interior Ministry said the conversation reflected the two countries' commitment to strengthening security and stability through closer cooperation. The discussion comes as Baghdad seeks to manage security along its borders. While Jordan and Iraq have positive historic ties, the desert area near Jordan and Syria in Iraq’s Western Anbar area has been a source of threats in the past. This is a largely tribal, sparsely populated area that could become a security vacuum following the US withdrawal from Iraq and Syria.
Iraq is also focusing on security along its western border with Syria. According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Defense Minister Nayef Mukayif al-Shammari conducted an aerial inspection tour on Saturday of Iraqi military units deployed along the Iraq-Syria border in Nineveh province. The Iraqi Defense Ministry said the visit aimed to review force deployment and positioning along the border and assess operational readiness.

articles.title: Rubio describes Russia-Ukraine war as territorial dispute ahead of November peace talks
articles.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared to reduce Russia’s invasion of Ukraine to a territorial dispute over the Donbas Region in comments to reporters last week.
"(P)eople keep talking about it's a war in Ukraine. That war is about Donbas. It's about one region of the country," Rubio told reporters during a visit to India last week.
"At its core, (the war) is about 11% of one part of that country that Russia wants and cannot take militarily and that Ukraine is unwilling to give up."
This comes after the US announced that trilateral peace talks between the three countries would take place in November.
In a major departure from US foreign policy, President Donald Trump waived sanctions for Russia and announced that the US would be purchasing Russian diesel.
Does the US understand what is going on in Ukraine?
But by framing the Ukraine-Russia War as a territorial dispute, Rubio’s comments could reveal where the Trump administration’s head is at before the talks in November.
It also signals that the administration has a profound misunderstanding of the war and Putin’s ambitions for Ukraine.
Putin said on Thursday that the territories in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow were "historically Russian land," raising stakes in talks to settle the conflict.
"Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia," he said.
Putin also said any future trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States and Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both Russia and Ukraine, adding that broader European security issues should also be discussed.
"The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said.
The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ready for talks likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives."

articles.title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
articles.body:
The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujarat’s Kutch district.According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. The fishermen were identified as Kadir Thaimor, Muhammad Mussa, Azgar Thaimor and Ahsan Jat, all residents of Chach Jaan Khan village in Pakistan’s Sindh province, according to information provided by the BSF.Sir Creek is a narrow, marshy tidal channel in the Rann of Kutch, along the coastal region between Gujarat and Pakistan’s Sindh province. The area is strategically sensitive because the longstanding India-Pakistan boundary dispute over the creek affects the demarcation of the maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea.The region’s shallow waters, tidal channels and extensive marshlands make navigation and border surveillance challenging. Fishing activities in the area can also lead to fishermen crossing into the other country’s waters, prompting apprehensions by security personnel.
The BSF maintains surveillance along the sensitive western border to prevent unauthorised crossings and other illegal activities. The latest apprehension follows an operation based on specific intelligence inputs, during which the four fishermen and their boat were taken into custody.
Aryan Singh is a journalist with The Times of India, covering breaking news, defence and global conflicts. An alumnus of the IIMC, he tracks the people, weapons and geopolitics behind the headlines, with a focus on India’s national security, military affairs and conflicts shaping the world.

articles.title: China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs
articles.body:
BEIJING (Reuters) -- The Chinese commerce ministry urged the United States on Saturday to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China, saying a proposed rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties.
The U.S. Treasury Department issued proposals on Thursday to update its outbound-investment security program, adding biotechnology to restricted sectors and expanding coverage of high-performance computing and hypersonic systems.
Beijing's commerce ministry said in a statement that the proposal "discriminatorily" widened China-related investment restrictions and intensified curbs.
It firmly opposed the U.S. proposal and reserved the right to take unspecified countermeasures, it added.
Beijing also said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties and ran counter to the consensus reached by the countries' presidents, who have met twice in the past six months.
The U.S. Treasury has said the measures, which do not only cover China, are intended to stop U.S. capital from supporting foreign adversaries' development of dual-use strategic technologies that could threaten U.S. national security.
The U.S. program had already restricted certain U.S. investments involving China in semiconductors, quantum technologies and artificial intelligence.

articles.title: From lawyer's office to kitchen: father of American soldier killed in Ukraine volunteers in Kharkiv
articles.body:
From lawyer's office to kitchen: father of American soldier killed in Ukraine volunteers in Kharkiv
Edward Wilton, the father of a fallen volunteer who served in Ukraine's International Legion, has moved to Kharkiv to help civilians. Every day, he helps prepare hot meals for local residents, including hospital patients.
Source: Independence Avenue Media
Details: Edward Wilton worked as a lawyer in Florida for most of his adult life. However, after the death of his son, who served in the International Legion, he also came to help Ukraine.
In January 2026, Edward retired and moved to Kharkiv for good. Now he works at the Pekelna Kuhnya (Hell's Kitchen) charitable organisation alongside many other volunteers from around the world – the United Kingdom, Poland, Japan, Sweden and other countries.
Every day, they prepare more than 1,200 meals for local residents, most of which are delivered to the city's hospitals.
Quote from Edward: "I returned to help Ukraine and to help out what I think is my country too."
Details: Edward said he does everything he can to be useful, adding that he adores Kharkiv, loves Ukraine and its people, considers it an incredible place to live, and now calls it home.
He previously told Suspilne Ivano-Frankivsk that he has Ukrainian roots. He said his mother had always told him that she was Ukrainian, Polish or Austrian, and that this uncertainty prompted him to research his family history.
Eventually, Edward discovered that his great-grandfather came from Kosmach, a Hutsul village in the Prykarpattia region. In 1912-1913, his great-grandfather emigrated to the US. Wilton raised his son, Edward III, with an awareness of his Ukrainian heritage and in keeping with Ukrainian traditions.
Edward said his family had kept some traditions passed down through his mother's family, particularly celebrating Christmas and Easter. He added that they had talked a lot about their ancestors' heritage.
Edward III had always wanted to become a soldier, but he was unable to complete his military training in the US. However, he spent several months training to become an emergency medical technician.
After Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Edward III travelled to Ukraine and joined the International Legion. He served in Company Bravo under the alias "Hans" and took part in complex combat operations, for which he was awarded the Order of Courage.
Edward said his son trained with various weapons, studied tactics with his unit and was very proficient with a grenade launcher. He added that Edward was one of the youngest in his unit and that his brothers-in-arms perhaps had more military experience than he did.
He said he heard nothing from his son about returning home until the war was over, as everything was connected to the war. His son had several opportunities to return home but refused, saying he had not yet earned that right. Edward added that his son believed he should do more than he was doing.
Edward said that his son was fascinated by Ukraine and did not want to return to the US.
Edward III died in April 2023 from a shrapnel wound. The 22-year-old soldier, together with his brothers-in-arms, came under artillery fire while moving out to positions in Luhansk Oblast.
Edward said his son really wanted to be in control of his own life. He recalled reading the Iliad with him when his son was a child, including the passage about Achilles, who had to choose between a long, uneventful life and a short, heroic one. Edward said his son had told him even then that he wanted a short, heroic life rather than a long, boring one. Edward added that this was exactly what had happened.
Now, a memorial plaque has been installed in honour of the fighter in Kosmach – the village that his father now calls home. After losing his son, Edward keeps the certificate presented to him for service.
Quote from Edward: "My son said he didn't mind dying, but he wanted to be remembered."

articles.title: Netanyahu shares AI-generated image of nuclear explosion in Tel Aviv, two days before election
articles.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared an AI-generated image depicting a nuclear explosion over Tel Aviv on Sunday, just two days before Israel's October 27 election, prompting criticism from opposition leaders who accused him of attempting to frighten voters ahead of the polls.
The image, posted on Netanyahu's official Instagram account, shows a massive mushroom cloud rising over a densely populated city, with an enormous explosion engulfing the buildings beneath it.
Accompanying the image, Netanyahu warned that Israel faced an existential threat from Iran and that the country's security depended on the outcome of Tuesday's election.
"The State of Israel is in existential danger that Iran and its proxies threaten us with. It is astonishing that nothing has changed, and more than that, everything has become more dangerous because of the existential danger posed by Iran and the axis of evil," he shared.
Netanyahu added that the developments and new findings required the public to "put aside the disputes and think only about the most important issue: ending the work in Iran."
The post did not explicitly identify the city in the image, though it appeared to show Tel Aviv.
Golan calls for Netanyahu to be kept off social media
Democrats chairman Yair Golan responded to the image on X, accusing Netanyahu and those around him of losing control as election day approached.
"The prime minister of Israel published an image of an atomic bomb over Tel Aviv," Golan wrote. "I ask that he be kept away from social media. The man and those around him have lost it. The pressure is mounting."
"On Tuesday, we will replace those spreading panic and restore security and sanity to Israel," he added.
Golan's response came amid a broader dispute over Netanyahu's handling of the Iranian threat, which has become a central issue in the final days of the election campaign.
Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of using fear to win votes
Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot also condemned the publication, accusing Netanyahu of resorting to familiar election tactics.
"Another fearmongering video from Netanyahu," Eisenkot wrote. "You are hysterical. As in every election campaign, once again the same method of lies and fearmongering."
Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of threatening Israelis with mass destruction after, he claimed, failing to achieve the objectives of the war against Iran.
"You have failed. In two days, the people of Israel will show you that at the ballot box," Eisenkot wrote.

articles.title: Royal Navy moves to buy U.S.-made Skydio X10D drones
articles.body:
- Britain’s Ministry of Defence opened a tender for Skydio X10D reconnaissance drones with an estimated value of about $160,700 excluding VAT.
- Bids are due Nov. 19, and the contract is set to run until March 31, 2027.
Britain’s Ministry of Defence has opened a tender to buy Skydio X10D small drones, the American-made reconnaissance quadcopter already ordered by the thousands by the U.S. Army, with an estimated budget of £120,000 (about $160,700) excluding VAT, according to a notice on the Defence Sourcing Portal.
The tender was issued by Navy Commercial, the Royal Navy’s procurement office at Whale Island in Portsmouth, and published on Oct. 20 under the Procurement Act 2023. It does not say how many drones the ministry plans to buy or which unit will operate them. Delivery is listed for the South-East of England.
The contract is short. Bids are due by Nov. 19, the ministry expects to pick a supplier around Nov. 26, and the formal notice lists the contract as running from Nov. 30, 2026, to March 31, 2027, the end of the British government’s financial year. The listing on the Defence Sourcing Portal gives a slightly later start date of Dec. 10. The tender is open to any qualifying supplier, is marked as suitable for small and medium-sized businesses, and will be decided on price.
The X10D is a compact, rucksack-portable quadcopter built by Skydio in Hayward, California, for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. It carries day and thermal cameras, uses onboard artificial intelligence to fly itself around obstacles, including in complete darkness, and can track a subject day or night. The drone can switch radio channels automatically to keep its link under jamming and is designed to hold its position without relying on GPS.
The X10D has been on the U.S. Department of War’s Blue UAS list of drones cleared for military use since May 2024. In March, the U.S. Army ordered more than 2,500 X10Ds for over $52 million, the largest single-vendor small drone order in Army history. Spain awarded a contract worth up to €18 million (about $18.7 million) for the drone in February 2025, and Norway followed with an initial tender worth 101 million Norwegian kroner (about $9.4 million) in July 2025.
The UK Ministry of Defence already has experience with Skydio. In May 2022, Defence Equipment and Support’s Future Capabilities Group awarded a contract worth about £3 million (about $3.8 million) for the company’s earlier X2D drone, delivered with British partner Marlborough Communications, after buying and testing 90 Skydio drones in 2020.

articles.title: Preparations Underway for Putin-Trump-Xi Trilateral Summit, Ushakov Says

Preparations have commenced for a trilateral summit bringing together Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov announced on Sunday, Oct. 25.
Speaking to Russian state television network Vesti and reported by news outlet Astra, Ushakov confirmed that Moscow, Beijing, and Washington have agreed in principle to convene the three-way leader-level meeting.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Right now, I can already state definitely that Moscow, Beijing, and Washington are in principle ready to hold it, and preparations for it have already begun,” Ushakov said.
The senior Kremlin aide indicated that the trilateral summit is being planned to take place on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit scheduled for Nov. 18–19 in Shenzhen, China.
Addressing parallel diplomatic tracks, Ushakov characterized a prospective three-way meeting involving delegations from the Russia, the US and Ukraine in November as exploratory in nature, describing it as having a “range-finding character.”
APEC summit and conditions for Miami G20 attendance
Ushakov also addressed the possibility of Vladimir Putin attending the Group of 20 (G20) summit in Miami, Florida, scheduled for December, confirming that the Kremlin has received a formal invitation to the gathering from Washington.
However, the aide stated that Putin’s prospective travel to the US remains contingent upon the operational progress and concrete diplomatic outcomes achieved during the November APEC meetings in Shenzhen.
Trump Eyes Post-War Business Ties With Both Ukraine and Russia
“For now, we are discussing the November summit in Shenzhen, but we have received an invitation,” Ushakov stated regarding the Miami G20 invitation.
Asked directly whether the decision regarding Putin’s travel to Florida depends significantly on the success of the trilateral summit in China, Ushakov answered affirmatively.
“Of course. But as I say: first comes November, and then comes December,” Ushakov emphasized, underscoring that diplomatic sequencing will dictate Moscow’s scheduling determinations.
Diplomatic controversy and international legal hurdles
The prospect of direct leader-level engagements involving Trump, Putin, and Xi unfolds amid acute sensitivity across European capitals regarding great-power diplomacy brokered without the direct participation of affected European partners and Ukraine.
Former Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk cautioned on Saturday that three-way arrangements between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing risk partitioning European security architectures, comparing prospective summitry without Ukraine to the 1938 Munich Agreement and the 1945 Yalta Conference.
President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently stressed that no diplomatic architecture affecting Ukraine’s sovereignty or borders can be concluded over Kyiv’s head.
The Kremlin’s confirmation of the Miami invitation also intersects with institutional pushback from EU officials and international legal bodies.
EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs Kaja Kallas and the European Commission have repeatedly criticized White House overtures toward the Russian head of state, citing state-sponsored hybrid sabotage operations across Europe and an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague charging Putin with war crimes connected to the unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children.

articles.title: Algeria senate approves sending troops to Niger
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Algeria senate approves sending troops to Niger
Algeria's upper house of parliament on Sunday approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger to "protect energy facilities", a senator speaking on condition of anonymity told AFP.
Any overseas deployment would mark a first since Algiers sent troops to support Egypt during the 1973 Arab-Israeli war.
The legislator said 148 senators in the 174-seat body voted in favour of the move. The parliament's lower house is set to vote on the proposal later in the day, likely to approve it as well.
The rare measure from Algeria comes as Algiers and Niamey strengthen security ties after moving earlier this year to repair strained relations and following a thwarted mutiny in Niger in August.
Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including in areas near the border with Algeria.
The neighbours, who share a 960-kilometre (600-mile) desert border, have agreed to deepen cooperation against jihadist violence, cross-border crime and trafficking.
"This decision marks a historic break with Algeria's doctrine of non-intervention in military conflicts beyond its borders," said Abdellah Akir, an international relations researcher.
"It's driven by the need to protect Algeria's strategic depth in the Sahel and to secure the future trans-Saharan gas pipeline," Akir told AFP.
The two countries have been working to build the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP), a vast project to export natural gas to Europe from Nigeria via Niger.
'Strong signal'
Akir said the measure also sought to "send a strong signal to competing actors, including Morocco and the United Arab Emirates" - two countries with which Algiers no longer has diplomatic ties.
Geoff Porter, an analyst with the North Africa Risk Consulting group, said the move was "illustrative of a shift in Algerian policy".
Algeria "had tried to maintain its national interests and exert its regional influence through its customary means - dialogue, international law, multilateral forums," Porter told AFP.
"But in a multipolar and transactional world, those don't work anymore. Instead, Algeria moved toward more tangible means - actual physical presence."
"Algeria is still committed to its foreign policy principles," he added. "It's just demonstrating them in a new way."
Earlier this month, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune signalled the possibility of military involvement in the Sahel country.
"We will protect Niger no matter what," he said in a televised address on 3 October. "There are countries, which I will not name, that have conspired against (Niger). We stand by its side."
"Today, we have interests," Tebboune then said. "We have reached agreements (with Niger) in the oil, mining and other sectors, and some are seeking to destroy all of this overnight."
Algeria's highly unusual measure to deploy troops outside its territory requires the approval of two-thirds of its parliament, according to a constitutional amendment from 2020.
Gifted warplanes
The vote followed a visit last Wednesday by Niger's Defence Minister Salifou Modi to Algeria, where he met with Tebboune and army chief Said Chengriha.
A military cooperation protocol was signed by the two sides, according to Algerian reports, but no details were given at the time.
The move also comes months after Algiers gifted four military helicopters to Niamey.
The warplanes were deployed at the request of Nigerien authorities, the Algerian defence ministry said.
Additionally, Algeria inaugurated a 40-megawatt power plant in June intended to supply electricity to Niamey and surrounding areas.
Algeria and Niger's relations had been strained for months following Algeria's downing last year of a drone from Mali.
The incident triggered a diplomatic row, with Niger joining fellow junta-led allies Mali and Burkina Faso in recalling its ambassador from Algiers.
Algeria and Mali have since resumed diplomatic ties.
Niger has been run by General Tiani since a coup in July 2023 that toppled the elected president Mohamed Bazoum, who has been detained ever since.

articles.title: Reuters: US sought to activate Starlink in Iran after strikes
articles.body:
Reuters: US sought to activate Starlink in Iran after strikes
TEHRAN – Successive US administrations have repeatedly asked SpaceX to activate or disable its Starlink satellite internet service in different countries to advance Washington’s foreign policy objectives, including requests to provide internet access inside Iran following US-Israeli strikes, Reuters reported on Saturday, citing six former senior US officials familiar with the matter.
According to the report, the administration of former US President Joe Biden asked SpaceX to activate Starlink in Iran during protests in September 2022 following the death of Mahsa Amini. A former senior official in President Donald Trump’s administration and another person familiar with the matter told Reuters that the administration also discussed activating Starlink in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in June 2025 and February 2026, with the stated aim of expanding internet access and communications for anti-government protesters.
The report said neither the Trump administration nor SpaceX had publicly confirmed whether the terminals involved in the latest discussions were activated. It also cited a February report by The Wall Street Journal that the US government had sent thousands of Starlink terminals into Iran.
The revelations come as Iran has formally protested the unauthorized operation of Starlink terminals on its territory, accusing Norway of failing to take effective action and raising concerns about the use of foreign satellite communications infrastructure by the United States and Israel.
Iran protests Norway’s inaction over Starlink
On October 4, Iran’s Foreign Ministry summoned Norwegian Ambassador to Tehran Paul Bjornstad to convey Tehran’s formal protest over the continued operation of unauthorized Starlink terminals inside Iran.
According to Iran’s Foreign Ministry, Mohammad Hassan-Nejad Pirkoohi, the ministry’s director general for international peace and security, told the Norwegian envoy that the United States and Israel were exploiting Starlink’s satellite communications infrastructure to pursue interventionist activities against Iran.
The Iranian official criticized Norway for failing to fulfill its responsibilities as one of the administrations involved in registering the Starlink network with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). He called on Oslo to take immediate and effective measures to halt unauthorized transmissions within Iranian territory and handed the ambassador a formal note of protest.
According to Tehran Times, the dispute had been under consideration by the ITU’s Radio Regulations Board since 2023. According to documents published by the international telecommunications body, Iran has repeatedly reported unauthorized Starlink operations within its territory.
The board has repeatedly called on Norway and the United States to take appropriate action to stop unauthorized transmissions, including by having the satellite operator remotely disable terminals operating without permission where necessary.
At its 98th meeting, the board concluded that there was evidence of unauthorized Starlink transmissions inside Iran and urged Norway to take measures within its capacity to stop them. It also asked Norway and the United States to explain why terminals operating without authorization in Iran could not be disabled in the same way as terminals in several other countries.
At its 101st meeting, the board concluded that Norway’s actions did not comply with relevant ITU resolutions and Article 18 of the Radio Regulations. However, it said it lacked the authority to suspend frequency assignments to satellite systems on the grounds that the administration responsible for notifying the network had failed to comply with the rules.
Tehran has maintained that the continued operation of Starlink terminals without authorization violates Iran’s sovereignty and national security. The dispute also highlights questions over the responsibilities of governments involved in registering satellite networks and the ability of operators to prevent services from being provided in countries where they are not authorized.
Starlink and US foreign policy
Reuters reported that the Biden administration also asked SpaceX to disable terminals allegedly used by Yemen’s Houthi movement and Hezbollah in Lebanon. Former US officials said the administration shared intelligence with the company concerning the possible use of diverted Starlink terminals by the two groups and requested that the devices be identified and deactivated. At least some terminals were subsequently switched off, according to two of the officials.
The disclosures have renewed questions about the extent to which US administrations rely on Elon Musk’s privately owned company to implement foreign policy and security objectives. SpaceX did not respond to Reuters’ requests for comment on the reported requests concerning Iran.
For Tehran, the issue extends beyond internet access to the regulation of satellite communications and the use of foreign technology inside Iranian territory without authorization. Iranian officials have repeatedly called on the countries responsible for the Starlink network’s registration, as well as its operator, to ensure that the service complies with international telecommunications regulations and Iran’s requirement for authorization.

articles.title: Israel needs sanctions-proof economy – Netanyahu
articles.body:
Israel needs sanctions-proof economy – Netanyahu
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said his country must prepare to adapt its economy to global sanctions, citing declining international support and a potential end to US financial and military aid.
Public opinion toward Israel has grown increasingly negative amid the wars in Gaza and Iran. In the US, a recent Chicago Council on Global Affairs report recorded the country’s lowest favorability rating since its polling began in 1978, with a majority supporting reducing or ending military aid.
Last month, the UK announced a ban on imports from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband describing settlers as “terrorists” supported by Netanyahu’s government and accusing them of ethnically cleansing Palestinians. The same day, 11 other countries, including France, Spain, and Canada, joined Britain in a statement supporting the two-state solution and announcing plans to impose or consider restrictions on trade with the settlements.
“We must understand that there could be sanctions, including banking sanctions,” Netanyahu said in an interview which aired on Israel’s Channel 10 on Friday.
“We need to prepare an alternative economy capable of functioning by circumventing these sanctions,” he added, noting that blockchain technology, which underpins cryptocurrencies, was among the options under consideration and that he had already requested an implementation plan.
The Israeli prime minister also expressed concern over a potential shift in Washington’s position, saying that “it’s only a matter of time” before US military aid is completely “over.”
“If you think we’re going to continue receiving what I secured twice, and that’s tens of billions of dollars in American aid for the defense budget, prepare yourselves and get used to the fact that it won’t happen because America has changed,” he said.
Under an agreement signed in 2016, Washington committed to providing $38 billion in military aid through 2028. Netanyahu previously said he wanted to phase out the financial component of US military assistance within ten years.
Former prime minister and opposition figure Yair Lapid seized on the remarks, saying that “Netanyahu now admits, in his own words, that if his government is returned to power, American military aid will end and Israel will face sanctions that will devastate our economy, trigger uncontrolled price surges, and cause irreparable damage.”
The comments come days before Israel’s first national election since the October 7 Hamas attacks, with accountability for security failures, the cost of living, ultra-Orthodox military service, and the country’s international standing among the issues facing voters. Neither Netanyahu’s allies nor the opposition have a clear path to a parliamentary majority.

Mass protests grip Western Europe (VIDEOS)
Mass protests have swept across Europe over the weekend, with demonstrators clashing with riot police amid widespread anger over soaring living costs and government policies.
The unrest has largely been inspired by the protests in France, which began in September. Spearheaded by students, they were originally aimed at rising education costs, a lack of teachers, and the poor condition of educational facilities. They eventually morphed into widespread violence and now carry a broader anti-government undertone.
France remains the hotbed of the protests, with at least 410,000 people hitting the streets nationwide on Saturday, including some 110,000 in Paris, according to Interior Ministry figures. The CGT union, one of the key organizers of the demonstrations, put the estimate nearly twice as high, at about 800,000.
The French authorities have implemented strict security measures in an effort to avoid a repeat of widespread rioting over the past weekend. In Paris, the demonstrators were banned from gathering at several central locations, ending up confined to the city’s southeastern edge.
The protests nevertheless turned violent in multiple locations, including Paris, where clashes between police and rowdy demonstrators were observed after the march concluded. Violence has been reported in Clermont-Ferrand, Lyon, Marseille, Strasbourg, Nice, Nantes, and other cities, where law enforcement used riot control measures to repel protesters.
