articles.title: The West’s double standard on global unrest
articles.body:
The West’s double standard on global unrest
Ideology, strategic interests and cultural ignorance explain why protests in Hong Kong and beyond are viewed through a selective lens
In the early days of the student protests in France, mainstream Western media took the protesters’ claims about poor school facilities and declining resources at face value. Only when the violence spread across the country, and to some of its European neighbours, did people begin to ask whether deeper causes were at play.
Leftists blame social problems, from the cost-of-living pressures linked to the war in Ukraine to rising unemployment, especially among the young. Right-wing critics blame Islamists, antifascists, radical environmentalists and, of course, immigrants.
A Financial Times report said: “EU regulators are examining possible foreign interference and disinformation campaigns around the French riots and outbursts of violence and looting in other European countries. According to security officials, pro-Russian and far-right social media accounts linked to previous disinformation campaigns have spread violent videos in an attempt to sow more chaos. Iran and Algeria are also suspected of being behind some of the messaging, experts said.”

articles.title: Marvel plans to collaborate with Israeli writers on new 'Zodiac' series draws online backlash
articles.body:
Another Israeli success story in Hollywood is drawing online backlash, as Marvel is set to collaborate with two Israeli writers on a new series, with the announcement already sparking hostile reactions on social media before filming even begins.
According to a report Deadline published on Friday, Ron Leshem and Amit Cohen have been tapped to write Marvel's upcoming espionage series, Zodiac, currently in development for Disney+. However, some social media users have already declared that they will boycott the series solely because its writers are Israeli.
The announcement quickly drew criticism online, with some users attacking Marvel's decision to hire the Israeli writers. One user accused the company of prioritizing political messaging over its existing shows, writing, "You canceled the second season of Wonder Man and the future of Daredevil just to shove Zionist propaganda down our throats."
Similar reactions appeared on Reddit, where one user suggested that the involvement of Israeli writers meant the series would serve as Israeli intelligence propaganda.
"Another show going straight into the trash. Espionage and Israelis in the same series. You might as well have advertised it as Mossad propaganda," the user wrote.
Some criticize backlash as undermining new series prior to debut
Others criticized the backlash, arguing that the controversy had already undermined the possibility of discussing the series on its own merits.
"And just like that, there goes any chance of having a positive discussion about the series online," another user wrote.
Leshem and Cohen are established figures in the television industry, with a track record of creating Israeli and international productions. Leshem was among the creators of the original Israeli version of Euphoria, which later became an international hit through HBO's American adaptation starring Zendaya.
The two writers have collaborated on several television series, including The Gordin Cell, Valley of Tears, Traitor, Red Skies, and Bad Boy, as well as the international drama No Man's Land. Their experience developing security and espionage thrillers could now bring a new perspective to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
There is currently no indication that Zodiac will address Israel, the Middle East, or the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Nevertheless, the writers' Israeli nationality has already become a source of controversy, despite the fact that no cast members, characters, or significant plot details have been announced.
For some viewers, even a superhero series seems to have become a political issue.

articles.title: Deal or more war? Trump threatens Iran, claims US control of Hormuz
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that Washington faced a choice between reaching a deal with Tehran and launching further military action against Iran.
"Do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off? That's the only question," Trump told Fox News.
Trump claimed US forces controlled the Strait of Hormuz, saying: "Remember, we now control the Hormuz Strait. They get nothing. Yes, we get everything."
He maintained that commercial activity through the chokepoint exceeded pre-war levels and described the US Navy's enforcement of the blockade on Iranian ports and shipping as "unbelievable".
Trump on Saturday suggested Washington could launch fresh military strikes or secure a comprehensive agreement. He questioned whether Tehran would honour any commitments, while asserting that either outcome would represent an American victory.
Control over the Strait of Hormuz remains a central point of contention in the Iran war, which erupted in late February following joint US-Israeli strikes, despite a ceasefire and a memorandum aimed at securing a final peace deal.
Taiwan and semiconductor trade
Addressing technology and manufacturing, Trump accused Taiwan of having "stolen" the US semiconductor industry through predatory pricing.
"They stole our chip business, all of it, 100%, because they made chips at a ridiculous price, and they just pushed them in," Trump said.
He added that stronger leadership in Washington would have prevented broader regional friction with China.

Russian Navy Disappeared From Mediterranean for Two Months for First Time in a Decade
Russia’s Navy had no warships operating in the Mediterranean Sea for approximately two months between July and early September 2026, marking the first complete absence of Russian naval vessels from the region in a decade, according to a NATO official.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Breaking Defense on October 20, a NATO official speaking anonymously confirmed that the alliance had recorded a significant decline in Russia’s naval presence in the Mediterranean. The last comparable absence occurred in 2016.
The official attributed the decline to several factors, including Russia’s reduced access to naval facilities in Syria, shortages of logistical support vessels, and the growing need to escort Russian commercial ships, including vessels associated with Moscow’s shadow fleet.
Russia’s naval operations were further complicated after Syria’s new government terminated Moscow’s lease on the port of Tartus in 2025. Although an agreement reached in August 2026 allows Russia to use military facilities at Tartus and the Hmeimim air base as joint training centers, its previous logistical arrangements have been disrupted.
According to Breaking Defense, Russian warships have increasingly been assigned to escort commercial vessels in the Baltic Sea and other European waters, limiting their availability for deployments elsewhere.
“These escorting activities take up valuable days at sea for the Russian Navy, and it places strain on their ability to generate naval forces for other missions,” the NATO official said.
Basil Germond, a professor of international security at Lancaster University, also highlighted Turkey’s restrictions on the passage of belligerent warships through the Turkish Straits, which prevent Russia from routinely rotating its Black Sea Fleet vessels into the Mediterranean.
Despite the decline, Russian warships returned to the Mediterranean in September. Germond cautioned that Moscow retains both the strategic interest and the military capacity to maintain a naval presence in the region over the longer term.
In May 2025, Finnish Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen confirmed that Russia had begun deploying military vessels to escort shadow fleet oil tankers through the Gulf of Finland. The move marked a new use of Russian military forces to protect commercial shipping in the Baltic Sea, highlighting the growing demands placed on Moscow’s naval resources.

articles.title: Democrats ready to sacrifice Americans’ well-being for ideology – guests to RT (VIDEOS)
articles.body:
Democrats ready to sacrifice Americans’ well-being for ideology – guests to RT (VIDEOS)
Democrats’ vehement opposition to the diesel deal that US President Donald Trump struck with Russia earlier this month proves they do not care about Americans’ well-being, guests have told RT.
According to recent media reports, a group of Senate Democrats are working on ways to block the arrangement that is meant to rein in skyrocketing diesel prices in the US, while a Republican Russia hawk has put forward legislation to nullify Trump’s efforts.
Speaking to RT on Saturday, American journalist John Varoli said that Democrats are engaged in a “political witch hunt” and so have no qualms about targeting a deal that is “in the interest of the American people.”
He predicted that should Democrats prevail in next month’s midterm elections, they would do “everything possible just to ruin this deal and to inhibit it” for purely ideological reasons.
American broadcaster Garland Nixon concurred that driven by “ideological anger at Russia,” Democrats are showing a disregard for the plight of American consumers.
“At this point, what we’re seeing [is that Democrats] are totally ignoring domestic issues, domestic policy, totally ignoring the working class, and they’re focusing only on foreign policy,” Nixon told RT.
He warned that if left unchecked, rising fuel prices could plunge the US economy into a “severe recession.”
Legal and media analyst Lionel told RT that opinion polls that predict a Democratic victory in the midterms should be taken with a grain of salt. He argued that American voters could punish the party for its efforts to undermine the diesel deal.
“This is political suicide to proceed with this,” he added.
Matt Weinglass, producer, director and host of The Homeless Left, argued that opposition to the diesel deal is driven by a decade-long political narrative vilifying Trump, which has taken precedence over the economic interests of ordinary Americans.
“It’s not going to help the American people. It’s going to help the billionaire class and the donor class, the people that have wanted to keep this conflict alive as long as possible,” Weinglass told RT. He also suggested that European leaders could join forces with Trump’s domestic opponents ahead of the midterms.
Former Democratic Congressman Dennis Kucinich argued that his former colleagues should abandon their longstanding hostility toward Russia and focus instead on ending the Ukraine conflict and the war with Iran, both of which have disrupted global energy markets and driven up fuel prices for ordinary Americans.
“There’s this animosity that has built up. And some Democrats are just having trouble letting it go, and they seize on every opportunity,” he told RT, dismissing the proposed legislation to block Russian fuel imports as “going nowhere.”
Rather than trying to derail Trump’s diesel deal, Kucinich urged Washington to redirect its resources toward domestic priorities. “We have problems here in America to take care of health care, retirement security, education, on and on and on,” he said. “That’s what we’ve got to be focused on, not on war.”
Since diesel is extensively used in agriculture and freight, its price has a direct impact on the cost of numerous other goods. Farmers and truckers are particularly vulnerable to diesel price spikes.
Amid global energy supply chain disruptions caused by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, as well as the Ukraine conflict, diesel prices have risen considerably in the US, hitting a record $6.50+ per gallon in September, with prices in parts of California topping $8 per gallon.
The soaring costs have become an increasingly pressing domestic issue for Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
Earlier this month, the US president stated that Washington and Moscow had struck a deal for Russia to immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to American and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November, another million tons shortly thereafter, and potentially another three million tons. Shortly afterward, the US Treasury Department announced a temporary waiver of sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing the fuel to be sold, delivered, and imported into the US until April 7, 2027.

Ukraine’s FP-1 Drones Fly 2,500 Kilometers Deep Into Russia, Set Major Chemical Plant Ablaze
Ukrainian FP-1 long-range attack drones struck two facilities in the Russian city of Omsk on October 24, targeting a major petrochemical plant and a logistics warehouse operated by Russian e-commerce company Ozon, more than 2,500 kilometers from Ukraine’s border.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Ukrainian drone manufacturer Fire Point on October 24, its FP-1 drones traveled more than 2,500 kilometers before striking the Omsky Kauchuk chemical plant and an Ozon logistics complex.
Omsky Kauchuk, part of Russia’s Titan Group, is one of the country’s largest producers of synthetic rubber. The facility accounted for approximately 25% of Russia’s production of butadiene-methylstyrene rubber during the first nine months of 2024.
Synthetic rubber is used in various industrial applications, including the production of solid rocket propellants. The plant also manufactures methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE), a gasoline additive used to increase octane ratings, as well as phenol and acetone.
Footage circulated by the OSINT community Exilenova+ showed a large fire at the chemical facility following the drone attack. The extent of the damage and its potential impact on production have not been independently verified.
Omsk regional governor Vitaly Khotsenko confirmed that drones had reached the city’s northern industrial district, where emergency services were responding to the incident.
Khotsenko subsequently acknowledged that an Ozon logistics facility had also been struck. According to the regional authorities, personnel were evacuated from the warehouse, while emergency crews continued working at the site.
Ozon operates one of Russia’s largest online marketplaces, with logistics centers responsible for receiving, storing, processing, and distributing goods across the country.
The Omsk attack followed another Ukrainian drone strike earlier on October 24 against the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant in Tolyatti, Russia’s Samara region. Both facilities manufacture chemical products used in industrial production, including materials associated with fuel manufacturing.

articles.title: Opposition leader says Netanyahu ‘no longer fit’ to lead Israel
articles.body:
Just days before pivotal Israeli elections, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said Saturday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “no longer fit” to lead the country, warning that his economic plan to counter potential international sanctions threatens national security, Anadolu reports.
On US social media company X, the Yashar party leader accused Netanyahu of turning his attention to “dismantling the Israeli economy for generations ahead” after “dismantling Israeli society and weakening the army.”
Eisenkot said Netanyahu’s recent remarks are “conclusive proof that he has lost touch with reality and moved into a world of delusions,” accusing him of proposing preparations to disconnect from the global financial system in response to Israel’s declining international standing.
“This is the madness of a man who is no longer fit to lead the country,” he said.
His comments came one day after Netanyahu said he had requested an economic plan involving alternative payment methods, including cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology, in preparation for possible international economic and banking sanctions.
Netanyahu expressed concern about potential sanctions, including restrictions on the Israeli banking system.
Netanyahu did not say Israel would withdraw from the global economic system. The characterization of the proposal as economic isolation formed part of Eisenkot’s criticism.
Netanyahu also warned that US military aid would not last forever, urging Israel to prepare for its possible end and to strengthen military self-reliance.
– Warning against economic isolation
Eisenkot mocked the proposal as “Bibicoin,” combining Netanyahu’s nickname, Bibi, with his proposed use of alternative payment methods and financial technologies.
He questioned how Israeli technology companies serving foreign clients would receive payments or attract overseas investment if they had to bypass international banking and rely on cryptocurrencies.
He also questioned how international acquisitions of Israeli companies could proceed if the economy moved toward isolation from the global financial system.
He warned that this course could prompt Israeli companies to relocate abroad, cause losses in savings and investments, and encourage citizens to leave the country.
Eisenkot said the consequences could include fewer jobs and reduced resources for healthcare and education, ultimately harming national security.
“This is not an imagined nightmare scenario, but Netanyahu’s plan for Israel if he is reelected” on Tuesday, he said.
“This is a real warning. Israel will not withstand another four years like these.”
-Controversial remarks
Netanyahu’s remarks also drew criticism in Israeli political and economic circles.
Israeli media cited an unnamed senior economic official who said that using cryptocurrencies and alternative financial technologies to circumvent banking sanctions would not achieve the intended goal. The official warned that merely proposing such an approach could damage the economy.
The debate comes amid mounting international pressure on Israel for its war on the Gaza Strip, settlement expansion, and occupier attacks in the occupied West Bank.
The UK and other Western countries have taken measures against individuals and entities linked to Israeli settlements, while concerns have grown in Israel about broader economic and diplomatic pressure.
The exchanges also come ahead of Tuesday’s Knesset elections, in which Netanyahu and Eisenkot are competing to lead the next government.
In his post, Eisenkot urged Israelis to vote for “a better shared future.”
The former military chief is one of Netanyahu’s leading rivals, with the two sharply divided on security and economic policies, the country’s leadership, and its foreign relations.
Israeli politics also remains deeply divided on responsibility for the failures surrounding the October 2023 attack, the conduct of subsequent wars, military conscription, the economy, and relations with the US and other Western countries.

articles.title: Bulgarians Vote for President as Black Sea Drone Strikes Escalate
articles.body:
Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia’s war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast.
Polls place acting President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, as leaders in a race of 27 candidates.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
While the presidency is largely ceremonial, Sunday’s vote has taken on added significance after a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast that likely killed some two-dozen international seafarers.
The strikes, which sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security.
Bulgaria has stopped short of directly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome “benefits the Russian Federation”.
Both leading presidential candidates condemned the strikes, but they differ over the broader war.
Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier.
“I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe. A reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and a clear position,” he said at a rally on Thursday.
Fresh Clashes Rock France as Protesters March On
Iotova, formerly vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Radev supports Iotova and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war.
A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria’s first elected female president.
“My opponents argue that there must be a war of attrition.” she told a rally on Thursday. “The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted.”
Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41% of the vote and Gyurov 28%. If no candidate wins a majority, a runoff vote will be held on Nov. 1.

Tehran, Bangkok underline enhancing co-op in ICT
TEHRAN – Iranian and Thai officials have highlighted the importance of expanding joint efforts in the information and communication technology (ICT) sector, boosting regional and international interactions, and developing a memorandum of understanding between the two sides.
Deputy ICT minister, Mohammad-Hafez Hakami, and Thai ambassador to Iran, Sake Nopthaisong, met on Tuesday, IRNA reported.
Highlighting the longstanding partnership between Iran and Thailand, Nopthaisong called for continued cooperation between the two countries.
The official went on to say that since he was appointed Thai ambassador to Tehran, he has been interested in getting familiar with Iran’s accomplishments and capacities in different fields like artificial intelligence, digital transformation, and emerging technologies.
For his part, Hakami said that since the Asia-Pacific Telecommunity (APT) headquarters is in Bangkok, Thailand plays a significant role in strengthening regional technological cooperation. He suggested benefiting from the capacities of the two nations to develop interactions.
The two sides underscored the need to draft and sign a memorandum of understanding to foster bilateral relations and technological cooperation.
GII 2026 places Tehran 65th among top 100 science and technology clusters
The Global Innovation Index (GII) has ranked Tehran as the world’s 65th-largest science and technology (S&T) cluster this year, according to a report released by the UN’s World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).
Each year, the GII identifies and ranks the world’s top 100 innovation clusters. Using a bottom-up, data-driven approach that transcends administrative and political boundaries, the GII identifies geographic areas with a high concentration of inventors, scientific authors, and venture capital (VC) activity. These innovation clusters often extend across multiple municipalities or subnational regions and, in some cases, span two or more countries.
Three metrics determine the top 100: the locations of inventors listed in patent applications filed under the WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), the affiliations of authors of published scientific articles, and the locations of companies receiving venture capital funding.
The GII 2026, under the theme “Powering entrepreneurs at the frontier of science”, examines how scientific breakthroughs become deep science startups and spinouts.
In addition to China and India, six other middle-income economies have clusters among the top 100, including Brazil (1 cluster), the Islamic Republic of Iran (1), Egypt (1), Malaysia (2), Mexico (1), and Turkey (1).
Tehran is the only cluster within Iran that falls within the top 100 innovation clusters in 2026. In 2026, Tehran had 405 PCT applications, 58,732 scientific publications, 107 venture capital deals, 0.0 percent Share of global PCT applications, 0.7 percent share of global scientific publications, and 0.0 percent share of global venture capital deals, making it the 65th largest innovation cluster and 88 innovation cluster by intensity, slipping down from 63rd and 85th, respectively in 2025.
The city’s estimated cluster population, PCT application per capita, and scientific publication capita amount to 7,852,733; 52; and 7,497 respectively, IRNA reported.
The venture capital pre-deals per capita is about 14, and the total innovation intensity share per capita is 0.097.
In patent registration, medical technology ranked first (with 19 percent share), followed by computer technology, civil engineering, and pharmaceuticals.
Top publishing organizations in Tehran are University of Tehran with 5,232 articles, Islamic Azad University with 4,081 articles, and Iran University of Science and Technology with 3,725 articles. A majority of published articles are in engineering fields.
In a recent global ranking by StartupBlink 2026, Tehran’s position has advanced by 20 spots, ranking 348 among the world’s most innovative cities.
Tehran is home to 96 startups, making up 81 percent of all startups in the country. Tehran has approximately 1 startup per 100,000 people. In 2025, the ecosystem recorded an annual growth rate of over 36 percent. The city is currently ranked as the 1st strongest startup ecosystem in Iran, having remained stable since 2025. At the regional level, Tehran ranks 11th in West Asia, having moved up 2 spots since 2025.
According to Iran Innovation Zone, the achievement is the result of strengthening innovation infrastructure and developing interactions among different sectors operating in the knowledge-based economy, Mehr news agency reported.
The report by StartupBlink has highlighted the role of Pardis Technology Park, the country’s largest technology and innovation hub, as one of the driving forces of Iran’s knowledge-based economy. The park hosts hundreds of knowledge-based and technology companies, creating business development infrastructure and providing a platform for enhancing cooperation among startups, investors, large industries, and institutions.
Moreover, hosting the International Innovation and Technology Exhibition (INOTEX) every year, Pardis Technology Park plays a key role in networking and connecting experts in the innovation ecosystem. According to the report, thanks to the capacities of Pardis Technology Parks, Iran’s startup ecosystem ranks 95 globally.
The Innovation and Prosperity Fund and MCI (Hamrah Aval – Iran’s first mobile operator) Ventures are the two other key agents that have developed Iran’s innovation ecosystem by facilitating the growth of technology and knowledge-based companies.
Iran ranks 58th globally in ‘Corporate Engagement’, an indicator that reflects the effective interactions between large industries and innovative and technological companies.
Fintech, the leading industry in Iran, ranks 72nd globally, 5th in the Middle East, indicating the country’s high capacity in the development of financial technologies. Iran Fintech Industry has 23 startups, representing 19 percent of all startups in Iran.
In the Global Startup Ecosystem Index 2026, Iran’s startup ecosystem is ranked 103 worldwide, holding steady compared to the previous year. The Iranian startup ecosystem ranks 10th in West Asia, having remained stable since 2025. It ranks right after Oman and is followed by Iraq.
The country has 118 startups, representing one percent of all startups in the Middle East. This equals approximately one startup per 100,000 people. The ecosystem grew by +54.4 percent over the past year.
